basis: Defining skeletal malformations include wormian skull bones and brachydactyly; cardiac disease belongs to the distinct ABL1 gain-of-function syndrome.
Cortical malformation with developmental disability and seizures; esotropia affects 30-79%. Incontinence does not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Urinary tract malformations and absent abdominal musculature define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is annotated at 80-99%.
Intellectual disability and ectodermal dysplasia define the syndrome; clinodactyly occurs in 80-99% and syndactyly in 30-79%.
Mature T-cell leukemia involving blood and marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 40-50%.
Hereditary prostate cancer affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary tract invasion is not inherent to the concept.
Posture-dependent renal protein excretion defines this generally benign kidney condition.
SRRM2-related developmental and intellectual disability; obesity in 7/22 does not establish direct endocrine injury. Ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Infection of orbital tissues posterior to the septum; associated sinus infection is a separate source disease.
External and middle ear malformations with meatal atresia and conductive hearing loss define the disorder.
Amyloid angiopathy damages cerebral vessels and causes defining intracerebral hemorrhage and dementia.
Thyrotoxicosis and hypokalemia cause defining skeletal muscle inexcitability and paralysis; nerve injury is not the mechanism.
Deafness, synostoses and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define disease; alopecia occurs in 30-79%. Dental anomalies at 30-79% omitted because of the cap.
Follicular skin disease with permanent pitted atrophic scars; reported heart block is occasional, below 30%.
Bronchiectasis, chronic sinusitis and nasal polyposis define airway disease; recurrent middle ear inflammation occurs in 7/7 assessed patients.
Inherited thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection; skeletal and pulmonary abnormalities are individually below 30%.
Mast-cell neoplasm; malabsorption, osteoporosis and hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly each occur in 30-79%; overt hepatic failure is less frequent.
Neurodevelopmental disease with ataxia and brain abnormalities; optic atrophy in 3/3 and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/2 assessed patients; samples are small.
Inherited focal dystonia with cognitive deterioration; torticollis reflects abnormal neural motor control rather than primary muscle disease.
Tumors arise in cranial or spinal nerves; ocular involvement applies only to a subset of this umbrella.
Congenital absence of a reproductive duct; associated renal agenesis is variably reported and not established at the 30% threshold here.
Cytochrome b5 deficiency impairs hemoglobin reduction and androgen steroidogenesis, producing methemoglobinemia and endocrine sex-development abnormalities.
Congenital cleft between the laryngeal airway and esophageal passage causes defining swallowing dysfunction and aspiration.
The principal BBS5 phenotype is Bardet-Biedl syndrome with retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; BBS5-specific renal damage frequency is uncertain.
Varicose dilation of pelvic veins is a vascular disorder, including when veins surround reproductive organs.
